stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Tap each of the six lens shapes. A bundle of parallel rays crosses the lens. If the rays converge to a point $F'$ on the right, the lens is $\textit{converging}$. If they spread as if coming from a virtual $F'$ on the left, the lens is $\textit{diverging}$.
stages.concept: A thin lens is $\textit{converging}$ when it is thicker at the center than at the edges (biconvex, plan-convex, converging meniscus). It is $\textit{diverging}$ when it is thinner at the center than at the edges (biconcave, plan-concave, diverging meniscus).

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Three lens cards labelled by shape. Drag each onto the correct bin — CONVERGING or DIVERGING. A wrong drop resets the streak; you need all 3 in a row correct.
stages.concept: The name of the shape encodes the rule: $\textit{convex}$ surfaces bulge outward (fatten the middle), $\textit{concave}$ surfaces curve inward (thin the middle). For a meniscus, the stronger curvature wins.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: Three unlabelled silhouettes. Read the thickness profile: thicker at the center or thicker at the edges? Drag each silhouette onto CONVERGING or DIVERGING. One shot per card — a wrong drop resets the round.
stages.concept: Only geometry decides: compare the thickness at the center of the lens to the thickness at the edges. Thicker in the middle $\Rightarrow$ converging. Thinner in the middle $\Rightarrow$ diverging.

labels.tip1: tap a lens to swap — watch where the rays go
labels.tip2: drag each card into the correct bin
labels.tip3: silhouette only — thicker middle or thicker edges?
labels.peek_prompt: Trace the outline: is the material thicker at the center or at the edges?

1.1: Tap each of the six buttons at the bottom to swap between lens shapes.
1.2: Watch the orange rays: some lenses bring them together to a point, others spread them apart.
1.3: The three converging lenses (biconvex, plano-convex, converging meniscus) are thicker in the middle. The three diverging lenses are thinner in the middle.

2.1: The label under each card names the shape — that is enough to classify it.
2.2: A wrong drop resets your streak to zero. Read the label carefully before releasing the card.
2.3: Biconvex, plano-convex, and converging meniscus are converging. Biconcave, plano-concave, and diverging meniscus are diverging.

3.1: You have no labels — only the outline. Look for the thickness rule from stage 1.
3.2: Trace a vertical line at the center of the lens and a vertical line at its edge. Which line is longer?
3.3: If the center is thicker than the edges $\to$ CONVERGING. If the edges are thicker than the center $\to$ DIVERGING. One shot per card.
